text:
If you book an appointment in advance, you'll likely have a long wait. If you want to proceed immediately, we recommend walking in before 7 am to get a queue number at the medical records counter on the 3rd floor. This will allow you to see a doctor that morning. Doctors start seeing patients at 9 am. If you get a queue number later in the morning (possibly after 9 am), you will see the doctor in the afternoon.

There are no appointments available for new patients on Wednesday afternoons and Saturdays. We recommend walking in on Monday, Tuesday, Thursday, or Friday.

1. Go up to the 3rd floor to get a queue number.
- New patients: Fill out a patient history form.
- Existing patients: Just present your ID card.
The staff will guide you through the next steps.
2. After receiving your VN slip from the 3rd floor, go down to the glass-enclosed room on the 2nd floor to have your blood pressure measured and wait to be called for screening.

I brought my child here for a dental x-ray because they have a large machine that can't be done at the clinic. The staff provided excellent service. There weren't as many people as I thought. I came on Saturday morning and had to wait in line for a short while. However, in the middle of the month, on Sundays, they are closed for cleaning for one day. You should call to check before coming so you don't come for nothing. (Open Saturday and Sunday until 3:30 p.m.) You can also pay with a credit card. It's great.

Explaining the details to new patients, along with cracking jokes early in the morning. The number of patients and waiting times are good. I want to know what time queue number 1 arrived. 6:15 AM, got queue number 9 😂😂😂 …

The appointment coordination system here is terrible. Originally, I had an appointment after New Year's at the usual time, but they suddenly called to inform me that it was convenient to come today at 7 PM. The staff informed me that it would be finished by 8 PM, which was strange and late. However, because they thought there would be a lot of people on the line, the doctor moved it as quickly as possible. We agreed to come today. The coordination team contacted us and asked where I was. I was almost there and on my way, so I tried to hurry as quickly as possible. But when I arrived, the person who made the appointment didn't seem to have talked to the person who called and didn't know anything. They told me to go take my blood pressure and wait a bit. Then, a staff member called my name to inform me that I didn't have to wait and the doctor had gone back. I came from Samyan and took Grab for over 600 baht. The other end of the line kept calling to ask where I was. They didn't talk or coordinate properly. I told them the problem, that I had come a long way, but they chose to have me make a new appointment card even though I was there. They didn't tell me to make a new appointment. The coordination and problem-solving with patients is extremely terrible. When I called and they found out it was me, I hung up. This is extremely terrible service for patients.

One of the x-ray staff members was very rude, as if they were asking for free service. I'm from out of town and trusted this place, so this experience was very disappointing. The costs weren't covered by the government's universal healthcare scheme; in fact, I'm worried that a clinic closer to home with the scheme would provide better care. And the staff member who issued the receipt for the jaw-related dental work also spoke disrespectfully to my mother. There were costs involved; we weren't asking for free service, just so you know.

Terrible. The process is unclear. I called to inquire and was told I could get tested until 3 PM. I arrived after noon and couldn't do anything. The queue was full. I couldn't get tested, and I couldn't even get an appointment. It was a wasted trip, time, and transportation costs.

text: At 11:30 AM on 30/10/2015, I called to inquire about tooth extraction and X-rays. A female officer answered the phone. She spoke rudely and did not provide any information. She only said that if I wanted to have my teeth extracted, I needed to have my teeth checked first. I told her that I had already had my teeth checked on 21/10/2015, the day I received free dental treatment. However, the officer said that it was not entered into the system and that I needed to go for a new check-up. I have no idea what your system is. Whether it is entered into the system or not, you should explain it better. What I wanted was to have my teeth extracted and to consult about X-rays. The officer should have been able to provide better information. However, the officer did not provide any advice or information at all. When I asked if I could make an appointment, she said that the appointments were for late May or early June. We come to have our teeth done, so we pay. We did not come to have our teeth done for free. We wanted to start the examination all over again. That is why I called to make an appointment. If the officer at the patient service point cannot provide any information or explain anything, they should consider forwarding the call to someone else who can explain the information.

The service behavior of the counter staff on the 2nd floor doesn't deserve even one star. Almost all of them speak without any politeness or respect. We're not begging for food, you know. This kind of behavior damages the image of Mahidol University. They just wear the university logo, but their behavior is terrible.

P.S. With so many cash-paying customers, I don't even want to think about what it's like elsewhere. And I don't know how many different counters there are – 2nd floor, 3rd floor, 2nd floor...
Terrible.
Comprehensive dental services, meeting the standards of the Faculty of Dentistry, Mahidol University, at affordable prices.

Hospital Review (Dental Treatment Experience)

After spending 5 hours in an appointment at this hospital, I decided to share my firsthand experience because over the past 5 years, there have been both positive and disappointing things.

Initially, the clinic I'd been going to since childhood recommended this hospital for root canal treatment. The first dentist who performed the root canal was excellent; the procedure was successful on the first try, and I was truly impressed. However, when I switched to another dentist for a crown, the tooth developed problems and eventually fell out. Fortunately, the second dentist admitted their mistake and sincerely apologized. The cost was over 50,000 baht for the first tooth (implant + denture).
Later, I had another tooth crowned. I remember the day of the procedure; the instruments made a loud "thud" that startled me. After returning home, simply biting into a mango caused the crown to break. I tried to book an appointment at the hospital, but they were fully booked, so I went to a clinic near my workplace, but that only provided a temporary solution.
After COVID-19 in 2022, I returned to this hospital hoping for a more permanent solution and chose a new dentist. However, problems persisted. This time, the dentist said the entire procedure needed to be removed and redone, initially stating they would not charge me. However, I was charged after the work was completed. Fortunately, I clearly remember the dentist saying there would be no charge that day. I argued with the cashier until they finally waived the lab fee, but they still charged me 5-6 thousand baht.

It felt like I jumped from the frying pan into the fire. I spent hundreds of thousands of baht but received service that was very disappointing.

Areas for improvement:
1. Accountability for expenses:
If it's a rework or correction due to a previous doctor's error, it should be settled within the hospital, not the burden shifted to the patient with the excuse of a different doctor.
2. Data recording system:
Estimates should be clearly recorded, such as using color coding on the bill or in the system, to prevent patients from wasting time arguing with cashiers.
3. Communication and service:
Some staff members spoke poorly and lacked empathy, even though the costs were comparable to private hospitals, yet the quality of service was lower.
4. Appointment system:
Difficult to contact, calls are often missed, and they don't call back even though they have patient information. This wastes patients' time and causes frustration.
5. Quality of treatment:
After the procedure, the teeth should be fully functional. The doctor said I could chew everything except tartar. But the truth is, even chewing crispy noodles can cause problems in less than 6 months.

Good things:
• All the doctors I met were kind and friendly. I can confirm they were Nice 👍
• They made an effort to take responsibility, although it wasn't perfect.

Conclusion:
I spent hundreds of thousands of baht but received service that was disproportionate to the price.
I also wasted time, suffered emotionally, and experienced mental health issues due to a substandard system.
If this were truly a specialized university hospital, it should be doing much better in terms of treatment quality, appointment system, after-sales service, and the attentiveness of its staff.

text: The receipt was incorrect, indicating "the patient didn't pay in full." When questioned for details, the explanation was unclear, repeating the same points about a receipt the patient didn't request. When asked about payment, the response was, "Just pay the difference." Could you please think before you speak? Is it possible for a patient to have had an incorrect data entry resulting in an inaccurate receipt? The patient paid the full amount as stated on the incorrect receipt, not that they didn't pay in full. I don't want any improvement in this argumentative communication style. I don't want an apology from someone like this either. Continue as you are; there are many more patients who don't complain. #Finance, Chakri Sirindhorn Dentistry#

I had an appointment this morning, September 18th, 2024. The dental service was excellent and very affordable compared to other institutions. However, I was annoyed by the inconsiderate behavior of those riding bicycles and motorcycles (one wearing a purple shirt) on the sidewalk from the parking lot. They were driving on the sidewalk and honking at me, forcing me to get out of their way. I informed the security guard, who told them to stop, but they ignored me. Please have the building management handle this.

The place is quite spacious compared to the number of patients.
It's not crowded. Parking is available in front of the dentistry building.
There's parking, but you might have to circle around several times.
The staff are polite and the nurses provide good advice.

From my experience taking elderly people to the dentist at many government hospitals,
I've found this place to be very skilled.
They're very skilled and thorough in their dental work.

However, they don't seem to like dealing with elderly people.
They're abrupt, cut-off, and emotional.

I've never encountered this anywhere else.
I won't be back here again.

This dental clinic provides comprehensive treatment. The dentists are kind and gentle, and give patients very detailed advice.

For those hoping to walk in as a new patient and receive immediate treatment, this is not possible. We have a very high volume of patients. Consider that each case takes an average of one hour, and we can only see a few patients per day. Therefore, you must have a medical history and schedule a detailed examination before a treatment plan can be developed. Once you are in the system, please attend all your appointments.

This is the best dental hospital, serving the public according to the principles of the King's philosophy. If you receive treatment here, everything will be completed satisfactorily, without any worries about unexpected complications or escalating costs. Thank you.

I had an appointment to get my dental splint put on at 9 am. I was told to arrive at 8:30 am to have my blood pressure checked first. At 9 am, the staff called me in and told me to wait another hour because the lab hadn't delivered the splint yet. Shouldn't they have tracked the order before the appointment, instead of waiting until the day and time to see the patient?

Today (02/05/2024)
I planned to get dentures. I got in line and was number 42. After taking my medical history, the officer told me, "You're out of line, so you have to come back tomorrow."

I'm giving 1 star for the security guards.
This hospital has a HUGE number of security guards.
But they just sit around, stand in groups chatting in the parking lot.
They don't help with parking or directing cars.
I'm so confused, why hire so many?
Their only job is to chase people away, telling them to find their own parking.
This is a government facility, so they should pay more attention to improving this.
So that no one can criticize them for using the budget inefficiently, like the politicians they themselves despise.
Wouldn't it be better to reduce the number of security guards and increase the number of male nursing assistants?
Most of the patients are elderly.
They have to push their own wheelchairs, awkwardly and without much strength.
Grandparents, please help yourselves for now.
The security guards are busy, standing around chatting in the large parking lot.

The doctor's service was impressive. There's a rest area with meals for those waiting to see the doctor. Regarding parking, it's recommended that patients be accompanied by a family member as the parking lot is far if you bring your own vehicle.

Outside of regular hours, you won't be able to get examined on the first day. Only appointments are accepted, and if you request an appointment, the waiting list may extend for months.
Even during normal business hours, you may not be able to get examined if there are no medical conditions.

The map pins are completely wrong, it's really confusing. Such a large government building is located in a completely different direction. Doesn't anyone bother to fix this? The correct location is on Borommaratchathani Road, outbound, opposite Mahidol University.

It used to be really good, I can't argue with that. Now, more people are using the service. I've encountered dentists who are repressed and come to vent their frustrations while I'm having my teeth cleaned. This is after-hours, and I have to pay for it myself.

The doctor is highly skilled and the equipment is modern. The only downside is that parking is extremely difficult to find. You need to allow at least half an hour to circle around looking for a parking spot.

The security guard was terrible. He just told me to find a parking spot elsewhere. I was a woman trying to deliver something very heavy, and he told me to find a parking spot that was a long walk away... What kind of person would do that?

Came to use the service.
The staff provided excellent service. Love it!
Two years later, they returned again.
